items.rule: The nth term of an AP is a+(n-1)d.
Consecutive differences are constant in an AP.
Set the target equal to the nth term and solve for n.
items.example: Verify the resulting n is a positive integer.

items.rule: Two AP positions give two linear equations in a and d.
Three consecutive AP terms can be centered as a-d,a,a+d.
items.formula: \begin{aligned} t_1 &= a-d \\ t_2 &= a \\ t_3 &= a+d \end{aligned}

concepts.title: 1. Definition of Arithmetic Progression
concepts.subtitle: First term, common difference, and AP check
concepts.summary: An AP is a sequence in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant.
concepts.trap: One difference does not verify the whole sequence.

concepts.title: 2. General nth Term
concepts.subtitle: Use a_n = a + (n - 1)d
concepts.summary: The nth term is the first term plus n-1 common-difference steps.

concepts.title: 3. Finding Which Term
concepts.subtitle: Find n or the first negative term
concepts.summary: Set a_n equal to a target and solve for n. For the first negative term, use a_n<0 and check the preceding term.
concepts.trap: Forgetting that term numbers begin with n=1.

concepts.title: 4. Determining a and d from Two Terms
concepts.subtitle: Form and solve simultaneous linear equations
concepts.summary: Use two known AP positions, subtract to determine d, then substitute to determine a.

points.text: Subtract for d; substitute for a.

concepts.trap: Using p or q instead of p-1 or q-1.

concepts.title: 5. Consecutive AP Terms
concepts.subtitle: Set up 3 or 4 consecutive terms
concepts.summary: Use a-d,a,a+d for three terms and a,a+d,a+2d,a+3d for four terms.

points.text: Four terms: a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d.

concepts.formula: \begin{aligned} t_1 &= a-d \\ t_2 &= a \\ t_3 &= a+d \end{aligned}
concepts.trap: Using expressions whose adjacent differences are not equal.
